Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Money, work & business · Civic life: news, government & the law

contract noun

a legal agreement

also sign a contract, contract of employment, written agreement, under contract

classical

Gai. Inst. 3.88: omnis enim obligātiō vel ex contractū nāscitur vel ex dēlictō
Traupman 163, 296
M-O s.v. contract
Levi–Bini p. 18

contractus, contractūs m.

noun, fourth declension

a contract

The jurists’ word, not in Cicero (Lewis & Short); Traupman uses it of a builder’s contract (cūrābō ut contractus cōnscrībātur, p. 163).

Examples

  • omnis enim obligātiō vel ex contractū nāscitur vel ex dēlictō

    for every obligation arises either from a contract or from a wrongGai. Inst. 3.88

  • Cūrābō ut contractus cōnscrībātur.

    I’ll see to it that the contract is drawn up.Traupman 163

Other words

  • syngrapha, syngraphae f. — a written contract to pay, a bond

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Mur. 35: ex syngraphā agere, to sue on a bond (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. bond (financial)

    The lexicon’s word for a cheque (see cheque).

See also agreement, sign, contractor, cheque.
